request: What impact did passing Obamacare have on the federal budget?

reply.reply:
CRS’s summary of CBO/JCT projections estimated that the ACA would reduce federal deficits by **$210 billion over FY2012–FY2021**; that was a projection, not a measure of what actually happened (CRS R41664, PDF p. 7). The same February 2011 baseline projected $1,042 billion in net insurance-coverage costs and $1,252 billion in new revenues and direct-spending savings over that period. A March 2012 baseline raised projected net coverage costs to $1,083 billion, $41 billion above the earlier estimate (CRS R41664, PDF p. 7). These findings establish the estimates, not the ACA’s realized impact on the budget.

[View the brief](output/briefs/case-20261025-153249-bc88.html)
reply.reasoning: The verified CRS findings directly answer the projected budget impact at enactment and later baseline update, while explicitly distinguishing estimates from realized outcomes.
